videos.script: Monday, twenty past eight, and the phone link at Parque Barigui goes down. {{outage}} Its docks keep recording bicycles as they leave and come back, but nothing reaches the server. {{buffer}} At eight fifty-one the link returns, and half an hour of events arrives at once. {{burst}} Now ask a simple question. How many rides started between quarter past and half past eight? {{question}} Count by arrival time, and the answer is wrong, with nothing to tell you so. Count by when each ride happened, and you have to decide how long to wait. {{two-clocks}} That decision is what this lesson is about. A batch job waits for the day to close, and then counts everything. A stream answers as the events arrive, and has to choose what to do with the late ones. {{batch-and-stream}} You build both, on three mornings of dock events. A nightly job and a backfill, then a consumer that remembers where it stopped. Then windows, a watermark, and a crash that counts a hundred and fifty-five rides twice. {{programs}} By the end you can say when a stream is worth what it costs. Most of the time, it is not. {{end}}
